# Transcriptomics

Preserve the requested method, contrast, identifiers, enrichment source, and
statistical population. These are parts of the estimand, not interchangeable
output formats.

## Differential Expression

- Match count-matrix sample IDs to metadata before fitting. Confirm the design
  formula, covariates, reference and target levels, and contrast direction.
- Use raw counts for count-model methods unless the named method specifies a
  different input. Do not treat normalized or transformed abundance as counts.
- Use the matched experimental control. Do not replace a vehicle, batch-matched,
  or paired control with another baseline unless the task defines that contrast.
- Preserve sample and gene identifiers through reshaping. Resolve duplicate IDs
  rather than silently collapsing them.
- Do not add a manual gene prefilter merely to reduce the table unless the task
  or named method defines it. In DESeq2, prefiltering changes the population
  available to independent filtering and multiple-testing adjustment.
- Apply a filter only after the statistic it references exists. For example, a
  shrunken-effect filter cannot be applied to an unshrunk coefficient.
- Match the measurement scale to the method. Continuous Ct, intensity, or
  normalized abundance does not automatically satisfy count-model assumptions.

For DESeq2, `results(alpha=...)` sets the target used to optimize independent
filtering; it is not merely a final `padj` display cutoff and can change adjusted
p-values and which rows are `NA`. For a fresh analysis, match `alpha` to the
intended FDR threshold. When reproducing a documented result table, preserve
its documented `results()` settings or defaults, then apply any requested row
filter to that table. Treat unspecified source settings as method ambiguity if
the alternatives change the requested quantity.

Separate significance testing from LFC shrinkage. In current DESeq2 workflows,
`lfcShrink()` replaces effect-size and uncertainty columns while preserving the
`pvalue` and `padj` values supplied by `results()`, unless options such as an LFC
threshold or s-values explicitly change the inferential target. If the requested
quantity only counts adjusted-p-value rows, preserve the fitted model and
`results()` configuration; do not create a second significance route solely to
apply a named shrinkage estimator.

When extracting a count from a result table, determine header presence and
column meaning from the file plus dataset schema or metadata. Some tabular
outputs store column names only in metadata. Do not discard the first data row
by unconditionally treating it as a header.

## Target-Gene Results

For a requested gene value, use the same fitted model, contrast, covariates,
reference level, coefficient, and shrinkage method named by the task. Inspect
fitted result names when software sanitizes factor labels. A target fitted value
is not removed merely because a later foreground or significance filter excludes
that gene, unless the task asks specifically for a filtered result.

## Enrichment Setup

Define before ORA or GSEA:

- foreground or ranked-list rule, including direction and thresholds;
- eligible universe/background for ORA;
- organism, identifier type, mapping source, pathway library and version;
- test, adjustment method, adjustment family, and significance threshold; and
- requested output field, sorting key, top-N rule, and stable pathway identifier.

Use one homogeneous identifier namespace for each enrichment run. After
mapping, do not mix mapped identifiers with unmapped source identifiers in the
same foreground or universe. Either drop and count unmapped identifiers, or use
the source namespace uniformly when the selected library and tool document that
they support it. Apply the same mapping policy to foreground and background.

Foreground and universe are different populations. A DE significance or effect
threshold may define the foreground while the universe remains all mapped genes
eligible after upstream experiment-level filtering. Do not narrow the universe
with a foreground-only threshold unless the named method requires it.

Use the multiple-testing family defined by the named implementation. For a
clusterProfiler-style ORA, correction is applied to the tested result terms
remaining after mapping and gene-set-size filtering; do not silently add
zero-hit pathways to that family. Do not compare adjusted values produced from
different families as if they were equivalent.

When the task asks for pathways enriched in the same direction across
contrasts, run the requested enrichment separately for each contrast and sign
with a shared eligible universe and method settings, then intersect significant
stable pathway IDs within each sign. Intersecting DE genes first answers a
different question. Do this directional branching only when the requested
quantity is direction-specific pathway enrichment.

For a top-term question, sort by the named tool's requested or documented
ordering, select the requested rank window with explicit tie handling, and only
then apply the term-name, ID, or category test. Do not replace a top-N quantity
with a count over all significant terms.

## Odds Ratios And Source Stability

- Define the ORA contingency table from foreground membership and the eligible
  universe before accepting an odds ratio.
- Library snapshots and services can differ in membership, mapping, background,
  hypothesis family, and odds-ratio definition. Use the source and version
  requested by the task; results from another service are not automatically
  equivalent.
- Prefer stable pathway IDs for intersections and comparisons. Use names only
  when IDs are unavailable and the match is unambiguous.

Before finalizing, verify the actual contrast, target field or foreground,
universe, mapping, library, adjustment family, and final extraction rule.

  "help": "<p class=\"infomark\"><strong>What it does</strong></p>\n<p>Uses DESeq2 version 1.40.2 to estimate variance-mean dependence in count data from high-throughput sequencing assays and test for differential expression based on a model using the negative binomial distribution.</p>\n<hr class=\"docutils\" />\n<p><strong>Inputs</strong></p>\n<p><strong>Count Files</strong></p>\n<p><a class=\"reference external\" href=\"http://master.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DESeq2.html\">DESeq2</a> takes count tables generated from <strong>featureCounts</strong>, <strong>HTSeq-count</strong> or <strong>StringTie</strong> as input. Count tables must be generated for each sample individually. One header row is assumed, but files with no header (e.g from HTSeq) can be input with the <em>Files have header?</em> option set to No. DESeq2 is capable of handling multiple factors that affect your experiment. The first factor you input is considered as the primary factor that affects gene expressions. Optionally, you can input one or more secondary factors that might influence your experiment. But the final output will be changes in genes due to primary factor in presence of secondary factors. Each factor has two levels/states. You need to select appropriate count table from your history for each factor level.</p>\n<p>The following table gives some examples of factors and their levels:</p>\n<table border=\"1\" class=\"docutils\">\n<colgroup>\n<col width=\"24%\" />\n<col width=\"37%\" />\n<col width=\"39%\" />\n</colgroup>\n<tbody valign=\"top\">\n<tr><td>Factor</td>\n<td>Factor level 1</td>\n<td>Factor level 2</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>Treatment</td>\n<td>Treated</td>\n<td>Untreated</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>Condition</td>\n<td>Knockdown</td>\n<td>Wildtype</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>TimePoint</td>\n<td>Day4</td>\n<td>Day1</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>SeqType</td>\n<td>SingleEnd</td>\n<td>PairedEnd</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>Gender</td>\n<td>Female</td>\n<td>Male</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><em>Note</em>: Output log2 fold changes are based on primary factor level 1 vs. factor level2. Here the order of factor levels is important. For example, for the factor 'Treatment' given in above table, DESeq2 computes fold changes of 'Treated' samples against 'Untreated', i.e. the values correspond to up or down regulations of genes in Treated samples.</p>\n<p><a class=\"reference external\" href=\"http://master.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DESeq2.html\">DESeq2</a> can also take transcript-level counts from quantification tools such as, <strong>kallisto</strong>, <strong>Salmon</strong> and <strong>Sailfish</strong>, and this Galaxy wrapper incorporates the Bioconductor <a class=\"reference external\" href=\"https://bioconductor.org/packages/devel/bioc/vignettes/tximport/inst/doc/tximport.html\">tximport</a> package to process the transcript counts for DESeq2.</p>\n<p><strong>Salmon or Sailfish Files</strong></p>\n<p>Salmon or Sailfish <tt class=\"docutils literal\">quant.sf</tt> files can be imported by setting type to <em>Salmon</em> or <em>Sailfish</em> respectively above. Note: for previous version of Salmon or Sailfish, in which the quant.sf files start with comment lines you will need to remove the comment lines before inputting here. An example of the format is shown below.</p>\n<p>Example:</p>\n<table border=\"1\" class=\"docutils\">\n<colgroup>\n<col width=\"20%\" />\n<col width=\"17%\" />\n<col width=\"25%\" />\n<col width=\"19%\" />\n<col width=\"19%\" />\n</colgroup>\n<tbody valign=\"top\">\n<tr><td>Name</td>\n<td>Length</td>\n<td>EffectiveLength</td>\n<td>TPM</td>\n<td>NumReads</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NR_001526</td>\n<td>164</td>\n<td>20.4518</td>\n<td>0</td>\n<td>0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NR_001526_1</td>\n<td>164</td>\n<td>20.4518</td>\n<td>0</td>\n<td>0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NR_001526_2</td>\n<td>164</td>\n<td>20.4518</td>\n<td>0</td>\n<td>0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NM_130786</td>\n<td>1764</td>\n<td>1956.04</td>\n<td>2.47415</td>\n<td>109.165</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NR_015380</td>\n<td>2129</td>\n<td>2139.53</td>\n<td>1.77331</td>\n<td>85.5821</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NM_001198818</td>\n<td>9360</td>\n<td>7796.58</td>\n<td>2.38616e-07</td>\n<td>4.19648e-05</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NM_001198819</td>\n<td>9527</td>\n<td>7964.62</td>\n<td>0</td>\n<td>0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NM_001198820</td>\n<td>9410</td>\n<td>7855.78</td>\n<td>0</td>\n<td>0</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>NM_014576</td>\n<td>9267</td>\n<td>7714.88</td>\n<td>0.0481114</td>\n<td>8.37255</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p><strong>kallisto Files</strong></p>\n<p>kallisto <tt class=\"docutils literal\">abundance.tsv</tt> files can be imported by setting type to <em>kallisto</em> above. class=\"docutils\" />\n<p><strong>Output</strong></p>\n<p><a class=\"reference external\" href=\"http://master.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/DESeq2.html\">DESeq2</a> generates a tabular file containing the different columns and optional visualized results as PDF.</p>\n<table border=\"1\" class=\"docutils\">\n<colgroup>\n<col width=\"7%\" />\n<col width=\"93%\" />\n</colgroup>\n<tbody valign=\"top\">\n<tr><td>Column</td>\n<td>Description</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>1</td>\n<td>Gene Identifiers</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>2</td>\n<td>mean normalised counts, averaged over all samples from both conditions</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>3</td>\n<td>the logarithm (to basis 2) of the fold change (See the note in inputs section)</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>4</td>\n<td>standard error estimate for the log2 fold change estimate</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>5</td>\n<td>Wald statistic</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>6</td>\n<td>p value for the statistical significance of this change</td>\n</tr>\n<tr><td>7</td>\n<td>p value adjusted for multiple testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure\nwhich controls false discovery rate (FDR)</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table>\n<p>When <tt class=\"docutils literal\">Log2 <span class=\"pre\">fold-change</span> shrinkage after DESeq2</tt> is set to <tt class=\"docutils literal\">normal</tt>,\n<tt class=\"docutils literal\">apeglm</tt>, or <tt class=\"docutils literal\">ashr</tt>, the log2 fold-change and standard-error columns are\nreported from DESeq2 <tt class=\"docutils literal\">lfcShrink</tt> for the selected single contrast. This option\ncannot be combined with the older beta-prior shrinkage option or with the\nall-pairwise-contrasts output. Shrunken result tables use <tt class=\"docutils literal\">lfcSE</tt> as column 4\nand omit the Wald statistic column because it is not part of the DESeq2\n<tt class=\"docutils literal\">lfcShrink</tt> result. When plots are generated, the PDF includes both the\nregular MA plot without LFC shrinkage and the MA plot with the selected LFC\nshrinkage method.</p>\n<p>Generic PDF plots use the regularized-logarithm transformation for datasets\nwith up to 30 samples and the variance-stabilizing transformation for larger\ndatasets. This follows DESeq2 guidance for medium-to-large datasets and avoids\nthe high resource usage of rlog when many samples are analyzed. This automatic\nselection affects visualization only; differential-expression results are\nstill calculated from the raw counts.</p>\n<p>By selecting <tt class=\"docutils literal\">Output sample size factors</tt> in the "Output options"\nselection box, the size factors used to normalize the samples can also\nbe output as a tabular file.</p>\n",

Count tables must be generated for each sample individually. One header row is assumed, but files with no header (e.g from HTSeq) can be input with the <em>Files have header?</em> option set to No. DESeq2 is capable of handling multiple factors that affect your experiment.
